so Semester 6 becomes a second category and Semester 5 stays intact as an archive.

Write it however you like. Re-running setup edits the existing pinned message

subjects.name: Computer Networks
subjects.syllabus:
**COMPUTER NETWORKS** — BE05000171
*Professional Core · 4 credits · 45 hrs*

**Unit 1 — Introduction to Computer Networks** *(8h)*
Network models, OSI and TCP/IP models, network topologies, transmission media, switching techniques, Ethernet, LAN technologies, IPv4 and IPv6 addressing

**Unit 2 — Data Link and Network Layer** *(10h)*
Error detection and correction, framing, MAC protocols, routing algorithms, RIP, OSPF, BGP, subnetting, CIDR, VLANs, switching concepts

**Unit 3 — Transport and Application Layer** *(9h)*
TCP, UDP, congestion control, flow control, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, email protocols, socket programming basics, REST APIs and web communication

**Unit 4 — Wireless, IoT and Cloud Networking** *(9h)*
Wi-Fi standards, Bluetooth, 5G architecture, IoT protocols (MQTT, CoAP), cloud networking, virtualization, container networking

**Unit 5 — Network Security and Emerging Trends** *(9h)*
Firewalls, VPN, IDS/IPS, cryptography basics, secure communication, SDN, AI-driven network monitoring, zero-trust networking, cybersecurity practices

*Books: Tanenbaum · Forouzan · Kurose & Ross*
*MSE-1 scope is pinned in #midsem-1*

subjects.name: Data Mining Techniques
subjects.syllabus:
**DATA MINING TECHNIQUES** — BE05000181
*Professional Elective 2 · 3 credits · 45 hrs*

**Unit 1 — Introduction** *(3h)*
Data mining, KDD process, functionalities, applications, task primitives, major issues. Statistical measures: central tendency (mean, median, mode), dispersion (range, variance, standard deviation), data distribution

**Unit 2 — Data Pre-processing** *(5h)*
Data cleaning, integration, reduction, transformation, discretization. Orange tool

**Unit 3 — Frequent Patterns, Associations, Correlations** *(7h)*
Market basket analysis, frequent itemsets, closed itemsets, association rules, frequent itemset mining methods, correlation analysis, pattern evaluation methods

**Unit 4 — Classification and Prediction** *(10h)*
Classification vs prediction, statistical-based and distance-based algorithms, decision tree induction, Bayes classification, rule-based classification, model evaluation and selection, Bayesian belief networks, backpropagation, SVM, linear and logistic regression, WEKA

**Unit 5 — Cluster Analysis** *(10h)*
k-Means, k-Medoids, hierarchical (agglomerative, divisive), DBSCAN

**Unit 6 — Hyperparameters & Explainable AI** *(5h)*
Tuning, overfitting/underfitting, XAI, black-box vs interpretable models

**Unit 7 — Advanced Techniques** *(5h)*
Web, spatial, temporal, stream, text and multimedia mining; distributed and parallel mining

*Books: Han & Kamber · Tan, Steinbach & Kumar*
*MSE-1 scope is pinned in #midsem-1*

subjects.name: Machine Learning
subjects.syllabus:
**MACHINE LEARNING** — BE05000211
*Professional Core · 3 credits · 45 hrs*

**Unit 1 — Introduction** *(6h · 15%)*
What is learning, ML vs traditional programming, AI vs ML vs DL, ML lifecycle, types of ML (supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement), types of problems, training/testing datasets, underfitting, overfitting, bias-variance tradeoff

**Unit 2 — Supervised Learning: Regression** *(6h · 15%)*
Simple linear regression, multiple linear regression, gradient descent, polynomial regression, cost function

**Unit 3 — Supervised Learning: Classification** *(9h · 20%)*
Logistic regression, decision tree, CART, SVM, Naïve Bayes, K-NN, PCA

**Unit 4 — Ensemble Learning & Model Evaluation** *(8h · 20%)*
Bagging (random forest), boosting (XGBoost), confusion matrix, accuracy, precision, recall, ROC curve, F1-score, k-fold and stratified cross-validation

**Unit 5 — Unsupervised Learning** *(9h · 20%)*
Clustering: partitioning (k-means, k-medoids), hierarchical (agglomerative, divisive), density-based (DBSCAN)

**Unit 6 — Advanced Topics** *(7h · 10%)*
Neural networks, reinforcement learning, ML tools: NumPy, Pandas, TensorFlow, Scikit-learn

*Books: Mitchell · Bishop · Géron*
*MSE-1 scope is pinned in #midsem-1*

subjects.name: Occupational Health & Safety Management
syllabus:
**OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH & SAFETY MANAGEMENT** — BE05000451
*Multidisciplinary Open Elective · 2 credits · 45 hrs*
*Part 1 of 2*

**Part A — OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH** *(12h)*
Classification of occupational health hazards, routes of entry of toxic material into the body, dangerous properties of chemicals and their health effects, hierarchy of hazard control (elimination, substitution, engineering control, administrative control, PPE).
Work environmental sampling and types, permissible exposure limits, threshold limit value, lethal dose and lethal concentration.
Ergonomics and its constituents, application to safety and health.
Occupational diseases from metals, dusts, fumes and chemical compounds.
Physical aspects of work environment: noise, vibration, heat stress, poor illumination, radiation

**OHSM — Part B: SAFETY MANAGEMENT**
*Part 2 of 2*

**1. Concept, Philosophy & Psychology of Safety** *(4h)*
Concept and nature of safety, philosophy of safety, terminology, total safety concept, safety psychology, accident causative factors, general psychological factors, salient points of the Factories Act 1948

**2. Safety Management** *(4h)*
Concept and elements of management, functions, management principles, safety management responsibilities, safety organization

**3. Accident Causes and Prevention** *(3h)*
Causation, accident problem, reasons for prevention, factors impending safety, accident prevention

**4. Electrical Safety** *(3h)*
Electricity and hazards, Indian standards, effects of electrical parameters on the human body, safety measures for electric works

**5. Fire & Explosion** *(5h)*
Fire phenomena, classification of fire and extinguishers, standards, fire prevention and protection systems, explosion phenomena and control devices, fire awareness signs

**6. Personal Protective Equipment** *(4h)*
Need for PPE, Indian standards, selection factors, respiratory and non-respiratory equipment

**7. Hazards & Risk Identification, Assessment & Control** *(10h)*
Hazards, risks and detection techniques, PHA, HAZAN, FMEA, HAZOP, hazard ranking (DOW & MOND index), fault tree analysis, event tree analysis, major accident hazard control, on-site and off-site emergency plans

*MSE-1 scope is pinned in #midsem-1*

subjects.name: Python for Data Science
subjects.syllabus:
**PYTHON FOR DATA SCIENCE** — BE05000231
*Professional Elective 1 · 3 credits · 45 hrs*

**Unit 1 — Introduction, Data Types & Operators** *(10h)*
Features and history of Python, variables and data types, operators (arithmetic, assignment, comparison, logical, membership, identity, bitwise), list, tuple, set, dictionary, string operations.
Decision making, loops and functions: if/elif/else, boolean expressions, while, for, nested loops, break, continue, pass, custom functions, scope, modules

**Unit 2 — File Handling & Exception Handling** *(8h)*
File I/O, text files, CSV files, binary files, exception handling, Python MySQL basics

**Unit 3 — Data Science & Descriptive Statistics** *(6h)*
Understanding data and its types, data science life cycle, data analysis (univariate, bivariate, multivariate), measurement scale, descriptive statistics (central tendency, dispersion, location, shape and symmetry)

**Unit 4 — Exploring Python Libraries** *(6h)*
SciPy stats, NumPy multidimensional arrays, Pandas, Scikit-learn basics, BeautifulSoup

**Unit 5 — Probabilistic & Inferential Statistics** *(5h)*
Random variables, PMF, PDF, CDF, binomial and Poisson, normal and exponential, sampling, estimation, central limit theorem, hypothesis testing

**Unit 6 — Data Preparation** *(5h)*
Loading, cleaning, missing data, duplicates, slicing and dicing, filtering, concatenating, sorting, aggregating, outliers, wrangling, normalization

**Unit 7 — Data Visualisation** *(5h)*
Figures, subplots, graphs and plots in Matplotlib, Seaborn basics

*MSE-1 scope is pinned in #midsem-1*

subjects.name: Web Application Development
subjects.syllabus:
**WEB APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT** — BE05000281
*Professional Elective 2 · 3 credits · 45 hrs*

**Module 1 — Introduction to Web Technologies** *(2h)*
Web technologies, evolution of websites, client-server architecture, frontend/backend/database overview, static vs dynamic websites

**Module 2 — HTML & CSS Fundamentals** *(9h)*
HTML structure and tags, tables, forms, media elements, div and semantic elements, CSS selectors and styling, colors, backgrounds, fonts, margin, padding, borders, flexbox, positioning, responsive design, media queries, Bootstrap basics

**Module 3 — JavaScript Fundamentals** *(10h)*
Variables and datatypes, operators and conditions, loops and functions, arrays and objects, DOM manipulation, event handling, browser local storage, asynchronous programming, callbacks and promises, Fetch API

**Module 4 — APIs & HTTP Communication** *(6h)*
APIs, client-server communication, HTTP request and response, status codes, query parameters and request body, CRUD operations, JSON and XML, integrating public APIs

**Module 5 — Backend Development with Node.js** *(8h)*
Node.js, runtime environment, npm, HTTP servers, Express.js, routing and middleware, REST API development, database connectivity, Postman, authentication and authorization

**Module 6 — Frontend Development with React.js** *(7h)*
React.js, JSX, component-based architecture, functional components, props and state, useState, useEffect, conditional and list rendering, API integration, CORS

**Module 7 — Deployment & Modern Web Concepts** *(3h)*
Hosting, domain management, SEO, CAPTCHA, cloud concepts

*MSE-1 scope is pinned in #midsem-1*
